page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Edsv6 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores running at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 472 GB disk, and the virtual machine is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. No GPUs are included.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core scaling presents a notable tradeoff. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory read bandwidth is also limited, with uncached large block reads measured at 37.14 GB/sec. Conversely, memory write bandwidth and Passmark database operations perform in the average tier. Large-model LLM inference is weak, with a 7B model generating only 4.5 tokens/sec, though small 135M model inference remains average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-4ds_v6 offers high memory density per vCPU, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require dense parallel compute scaling. The inclusion of 472 GB of local storage reduces the immediate need for external storage attachments for local caching. This hardware profile is suited for relational database operations, text processing tasks, and static web serving, where single-core performance and memory capacity are prioritized over highly parallelized multi-core execution.
